key_findings: The primary hypothesis is that microgravity conditions fundamentally alter combustion and extinction characteristics of liquid fuel droplets.
The goal is to map flammability boundaries, quantify suppressant efficacy, and develop predictive models to improve fire safety in space environments.
fields.earth_applications: The insights gained from these experiments have the potential to advance fire safety in confined and reduced-gravity environments on Earth.

evidence: Select the test pressure (0.5 − 1.5 atm) for the LOI tests.

conditions.label: Methanol droplet combustion in oxygen-nitrogen-carbon dioxide at 0.7 atm
evidence: Spray and Droplet Results Over one hundred methanol droplet tests in varying diluent concentrations and at primarily two different ambient pressures (0.7 and 1 atm) have been performed to date. In these tests the oxygen concentration varied from 30% to 12% by volume while the carbon dioxide and helium diluent concentrations varied in the range of 0% to 70% by volume and the rest of the inert was nitrogen.

conditions.label: n-decane droplets, 0.5 atm pressure, 21% O2 and 79% N2
evidence: Figure 1a (R377) corresponds to a n-decane droplet with an initial diameter of 4.03 mm burning in 21% oxygen and 79% nitrogen mixture at 0.5 atm pressure.

conditions.label: n-decane droplets, 0.5 atm pressure, 25% O2 and 75% N2
evidence: Figure 1b (R374) shows the combustion characteristics for a 3.79 mm n-decane droplet burning at a slightly increased oxygen concentration of 25% and the rest being nitrogen at 0.5 atm pressure.

conditions.label: n-decane droplets, 0.5 atm pressure, 17% O2 and 83% N2

paper_findings.text: The limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluent gases is around 12% to 13% oxygen by volume.
When the initial droplet diameter is greater than roughly 4 mm, the droplet flame extinguishes through excessive radiative heat loss.
Large n-alkane droplets exhibited quasi-steady low-temperature burning and extinction following radiative extinction of the visible flame
Smaller droplets burned to completion or disruptively extinguished

conditions.label: Methanol droplet combustion in oxygen-nitrogen-carbon dioxide at 0.7 atm
evidence: The ambient oxygen concentration varied from a high value of 30% by volume to as low as 12%, approaching the limiting oxygen index for the fuel.

In these experiments, both freely ﬂoated and tethered droplets were ignited using symmetrically opposed hot-wire igniters and the burning histories were recorded onboard using digital cameras, downlinked later to the ground for analysis.

In these experiments, both freely ﬂoated and tethered droplets were ignited using symmetrically opposed hot-wire igniters and the burning histories were recorded onboard using digital cameras, downlinked later to the ground for analysis.

key_findings: The limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluent gases is around 12% to 13% oxygen by volume.
When the initial droplet diameter is greater than roughly 4 mm, the droplet flame extinguishes through excessive radiative heat loss.
